<reason>PRO kept the motion’s actual comparison live: easier pause/split/remix versus cable-style traps, not a promise of cheap catalogs forever. CON’s production economics were the strongest single argument in the room, but they repeatedly treated an option as if it were universal peak-hopping and never showed why a stay-put discount plus a click to drop an idle seat is infeasible. PRO’s pressure questions exposed that tension; CON answered it only by narrowing to a 5–10% threshold that still left lock-in looking like a policy, not a constraint.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s R2 collapse of CON’s two questions (rare pause cannot threaten commissioning; common pause only proves the cheap sticker needed idle seats) versus CON’s best hit that idle months are cheap to serve but costly to buy.</best_rebuttal>
